title: Synthesis of Monocyte-targeting Peptide Amphiphile Micelles for Imaging of Atherosclerosis
protocol: Weigh out 0.25 mmol of Fmoc-L-Lys(Boc)-Wang in a reaction vessel (RV).
Rinse the side of the RV with 5 mL dimethylforamide (DMF) in a chemical fume hood.
Load the RV onto an automated benchtop peptide synthesizer.
Load pre-packaged amino acid vials, N'-CYNFTINRKISVQRLASYRRITSS-C', from the C to N-terminus.
Include an empty vial at the end for the final deprotection step.
Transfer peptides on resin from the RV to a scintillation vial with 2-3 mL methanol until all of the resins are transferred.
Remove the methanol supernatant and evaporate the remaining liquid until dry.
Vacuum dry the residue for an additional 2 h or overnight at room temperature.
Make 12 mL cleavage solution containing trifluoracetic acid (TFA):ethanedithiol:water:triisopropylsilane at 94:2.5:2.5:1 vol% in a chemical fume hood.
Swirl the cleavage solution to make sure it is evenly mixed.
Place the synthesis vessel onto an arm shaker by clamping near the bottom half.
Transfer peptide-resin to the SV with 2 mL of cleavage solution until all are transferred.
Wash the sides of the SV with 3 mL cleavage solution.
Close the cap of the SV and shake at 300 oscillations/min for 4 h.
Weigh out an empty 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Record the mass.
Drain the cleaved peptide solution from the SV into the 50 mL centrifuge tube after 4 h.
Rinse the SV several times with the remaining cleavage solution.
Evaporate cleaved peptide solution with nitrogen until there is less than 4 mL remaining.
Add 36 mL of ice-cold ether to the peptide-cleaved solution.
Vortex the solution until it is completely white or yellow.
Centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Decant the supernatant.
Add 40 mL ice-cold ether to the tube.
Vortex and sonicate again.
Repeat the centrifugation process.
Decant the supernatant.
Dry the crude PA pellet with nitrogen gas purging until the ether is visibly evaporated.
Add 20 mL double-distilled water, vortex, and sonicate until the peptide is completely dissolved in solution.
Freeze the solution and lyophilize until dry.
Once the peptide is dried, weigh out the mass of the centrifuge tube containing the crude peptide.
Dissolve the crude peptide in 5 mg/mL water.
Dissolve 25 mg of crude MCP-1 peptide in 5 mL double-distilled water to make a total concentration of 5 mg/mL.
Purify the crude MCP-1 peptide by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) using 0.1% TFA in water and 0.1% TFA in acetonitrile as mobile phases on a C8 reverse-phase column.
Inject the 5 mL of the peptide into the HPLC.
Decrease solvent A slowly to 30% over 27 min and hold at this composition for 3 min.
Return the gradient to 100% solvent A over 3 min and hold at this composition for 1 min.
Keep the column temperature at 55 °C during the run.
Analyze each fraction using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) mass spectrometry for the expected product m/z at 2,890.
Dissolve α-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid at 1 mg/mL in acetonitrile/water (50:50 vol%) as the matrix solution.
Spot 0.75 µL of matrix solution onto the MALDI plate.
Spot 0.75 µL of each fraction on top of the matrix spot.
Carry out the analysis using a positive reflective ion mode at a mass range of 500-5,000 Da.
Combine product fractions after HPLC purification.
Blow off acetonitrile from combined fractions.
Freeze and lyophilize purified peptides until dry.
Prepare a 1.1 molar excess of DSPE-PEG(2000)-maleimide to peptide in separate scintillation vials.
Dissolve both compounds in double-distilled water to make ~15 mg/mL.
Sonicate for 15 minutes or until solutions are completely clear.
Add the DSPE-PEG(2000)-maleimide solution to the peptide solution.
Vortex and sonicate the mixture.
Add 1 M NaOH dropwise (1 µL at a time) until the pH of the solution is 7.
Purge the solution with nitrogen for 5 minutes.
Stir the solution overnight.
Freeze the solution and lyophilize until dry.
Dissolve the dried solid in 5 mg/mL water.
Purify the solution with HPLC as described above.
Analyze each fraction using MALDI mass spectrometry for the corresponding m/z.
Dissolve 1.75 mg MCP-1 PAs with 3 mL methanol in a 1-dram vial.
Sonicate until the MCP-1 PA is completely dissolved.
Evaporate the methanol under nitrogen in a circular motion while rinsing the remaining methanol off the side of the vial until a uniform film is formed at the bottom of the vial.
Vacuum-dry the film overnight.
Hydrate the dried film with 3 mL of water or phosphate buffer saline (PBS) to make a 100 µM solution of MCP-1 PAMs.
Gently vortex and sonicate the solution until clear.
Incubate at 80 °C for 30 min.
Cool the resulting dispersion to room temperature.
Place 100 µM of MCP-1 PAM or scrambled PAM in a cuvette according to the instrument's instructions for DLS or zeta potential measurements.
Equilibrate the instrument to room temperature.
Measure the size and surface charge of the PAM.
Add 7 µL of 50 µM MCP-1 PAM or scrambled PAM onto a TEM grid suspended within a self-closing tweezer for 5 min.
Wick away the droplet with a delicate task wipe.
Add 7 µL of water to wash the grid.
Wick away the droplet.
Add 7 µL of 1 wt% phosphotungstic acid for 2 min.
Wick away the droplet.
Repeat step 2.2.2.
Dry the TEM grid prior to TEM analysis.
Turn on the nitrogen for 5-10 min prior to use of the instrument.
Place 300 µL of blank (water or PBS) in cuvette.
Measure spectra at 190-265 nm, 0.2 mm path-length with a 1 s integration time, and a 1 nm bandwidth in room temperature.
Collect 3 replicates.
Measure 100 µM MCP-1 peptide, MCP-1 PAM, scrambled peptide, and scrambled PAM under the same condition described in step 2.3.3.
Subtract from the blank.
Fit the data using a linear interpolation of polylysine basis spectra.
Turn off the instrument.
Wait 10 min before turning off the nitrogen.

Culture and expand WEHI 274.1 murine monocytes in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 0.05 mM 2-mercaptoethanol in 37 °C under 5% CO2 to passage 5.
Pipet monocytes in media into a sterile 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the old media.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL of fresh media in a centrifuge tube.
Mix slowly until cells are evenly distributed in the media.
Count the cells using trypan blue staining and a hemocytometer.
Dilute cells to obtain 4,000 monocytes per 90 µL of media per well.
Add 90 µL of diluted cells to each well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate for 24 hours.
Avoid using the wells on the exterior edge of the plate.
Fill the exterior wells with 100 µL PBS.
Dissolve 0.15 µmol of MCP-1 peptide, MCP-1 PAM, scrambled peptide, or scrambled-PAM in 150 µL PBS in separate sterilized microcentrifuge tubes.
Perform serial dilution to make 65 µL of each sample at concentrations of 1 µM, 10 µM, and 100 µM.
Add 10 µL of each concentration to the wells containing WEHI 274.1 (total volume: 100 µL per well).
Incubate for 72 hours.
Add 10 µL of MTS to each well.
Incubate for 1 hour.
Analyze the absorbance using a plate reader at 490 nm or based on the manufacturer's instructions.
Seed 500,000 monocytes in each well of a 6-well plate in 2 mL of media containing 100 µM Cy5-labeled MCP-1 PAM (10:90 molar ratio of DSPE-PEG(2000)-Cy5 and MCP-1 PA).
Incubate for 1 hour.
Collect WEHI 274.1 by centrifugation at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Aspirate the media.
Resuspend and wash the cells in 2 mL PBS.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the PBS from the centrifuged cells.
Repeat the washing process with 2 mL PBS.
Aspirate the PBS after the second wash.
Add 2 mL of cold 4% paraformaldehyde to fix the cells.
Incubate the fixed cells at room temperature for 10 min.
Pipette the fixed cells onto a sterile glass coverslip within wells of a 6-well plate.
Centrifuge the coverslips at 400 x g for 5 min.
Remove the paraformaldehyde from the coverslips.
Wash and rinse the coverslips with 2 mL PBS once.
Resuspend the cells on the coverslip in 1 mL of a solution (note: incomplete).
Put 10 μL of 90% glycerol in PBS onto a slide.
Use a needle and tweezer to pick up the coverslip carefully.
Dry the edge of the coverslip.
Gently place the coverslip onto a slide facedown.
Gently seal the edge of the coverslip with clear nail polish.
Place the prepared slide in the refrigerator until ready for imaging.
